title: Scale controller surge misclassification and cold-start mitigation
creator: Sofia Mendes
description:
Summary:
During a customer-impacting capacity event on 2026-02-18 we observed a short-lived traffic surge trigger an overly aggressive scale-down shortly after the burst, causing a wave of cold-starts and amplified request latency for 18 minutes. The incident was not caused by infra outage but by the scale controller misclassifying transient bursts as sustained load drop because of a smoothing/percentile mismatch in our KEDA adapter and HPA config.

Impact:
- Duration: ~18 minutes impacting 4% of API requests for the hosted API in us-west-2
- Symptoms: increased P95/P99 latency, token generation timeouts for long-context requests, elevated error rates reported by customers integrated with dedicated pools
- Customer-visible: degraded tail latency for serving and a handful of timeouts reported to support (severity: P1 for impacted customers)

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-18 02:14 UTC: brief traffic surge related to an external sync job (10x baseline for ~90s)
- 02:16 UTC: KEDA scaler observed rate spike and then rapid decline; 95th-percentile smoothing window caused the controller to mark load as low at 02:18
- 02:19 UTC: HPA initiated scale-down (pod termination + warm-pool eviction) while inflight requests still present
- 02:22-02:35 UTC: Cold-starts and KV-cache warmup overhead increased per-request latency; alerts fired for latency SLO breaches
- 02:36 UTC: Automated fallback and operator intervention applied warm-pool holdoff, system stabilized

Root cause analysis (short):
1) Smoothing window mismatch: the KEDA adapter used a 5m percentile-based smoothing (95th Pctl) intended to filter noise; that window is too long for short high-amplitude bursts and can invert the controller view once the burst ends, leading to a premature scale-down when backend pods are still serving queued/long-running requests.
2) Warm-pool eviction race: our warm-pool eviction policy was tied to pod termination lifecycle hooks and a label sync that lagged ~10s behind actual scale events; if the controller decided to scale down, warm instances were reclaimed before new pods completed KV cache priming.
3) Telemetry blind spot: we lacked a lightweight 'time-to-first-token' (TTFT) or readiness-continuity metric surfaced to the scaler to account for long-inflight requests; the scaler decision relied only on request-rate metrics.

Why previous mitigations didn't catch this:
- Earlier tuning focused on preventing chronic flapping (overreacting to noisy, low-intensity traffic). That made the smoothing conservative but inadvertently caused misclassification for short sharp bursts that have asymmetric ramp-down characteristics.

Immediate mitigations applied (done during incident):
- Increased warm-pool holdoff to 3m for affected pools to avoid immediate eviction (operator applied).
- Temporarily disabled aggressive scale-down gate in the KEDA adapter for the service during the incident window.
- Support notified and customers affected were offered incident summaries and a small credit.

Proposed permanent fixes and rationale (action items):
1) Adjust controller smoothing logic (owner: Ravi Patel, estimate: 3): change from single 95th-percentile over 5m to an adaptive dual-window approach: short-window (30s) for spike detection + long-window (5m) percentile for trend. This reduces misclassification for fast bursts while still preventing flapping.
2) Add TTFT metric to scaler decision (owner: Marcus Chen, estimate: 3): emit a lightweight histogram (bucketed 0-500ms, 500ms-2s, 2s+) per model-family and surface a derived 'active_warm_fraction' metric for the scaler to prefer avoiding scale-down when fraction < 80%.
3) Warm-pool lifecycle fix (owner: Lena Ortiz, estimate: 2): remove dependency on eventual label sync; use immediate pre-stop hook that signals warm-pool coordinator to pause eviction for X seconds if in-service requests exist.
4) Safe scale-down circuit-breaker (owner: Priya Kapoor, estimate: 2): implement a short cooldown that checks inflight request counts and KV-cache primed fraction before allowing scale-down beyond N pods.
5) E2E regression tests and chaos scenario (owner: Eng QA team, estimate: 5): add an automated test that replays a 90s 10x spike and validates no meaningful tail latency regression and no more than 10% pod churn.
6) Dashboards & runbook updates (owner: DataViz team / Oncall Docs, estimate: 2): add TTFT chart, scale-decision exploration panel, and a new runbook section for 'surge-misclassification'.
7) Release & rollout plan: bundle controller fixes into runtime-1.24 with canary rollout to 3 clusters, monitor 1-week before global promotion.

Acceptance criteria (for done):
- New adaptive smoothing is live behind feature flag and validated in canary with synthetic spikes
- TTFT metric emitted and visible on dashboard; scaler uses it to block scale-down when warm-fraction < 80%
- Warm-pool eviction race reproduced in staging and resolved by pre-stop hook change
- E2E test added and green in CI
- Runbook and SLO alerts updated

References and artifacts:
- Incident Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1676712345000000
- Grafana incident dashboard (latency + scale decisions): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/scale-surge/scale-surge-incident
- Confluence postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RE/ENG-75894+postmortem
- PR for temporary hotfix applied during incident: https://github.com/redwood-inference/keda-adapter/pull/412
- Proposed implementation doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C4D5E6F/proposed-adaptive-smoothing

Notes on trade-offs:
- Shortening smoothing aggressively reduces missed flaps but reintroduces noise; the dual-window approach aims to balance both.
- Adding TTFT metric increases cardinality slightly (by model-family) but is lightweight buckets and provides high leverage to avoid cold-start cascades.

Next steps (short term):
- [Ravi] open implementation PR for adaptive smoothing (due 2026-02-26)
- [Marcus] prototype TTFT exporter and dashboard panel (due 2026-03-03)
- [Lena] update warm-pool coordinator with pre-stop signal (due 2026-03-04)
- [Priya] design circuit-breaker gating rules and add to canary config (due 2026-03-07)
- After canary validation, schedule runtime-1.24 cut (tentative 2026-03-15)
